item.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine hit 2 Russian ships off Libya, and 1 sank
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was behind attacks on two Russian warships off Libya, and one sank.

item.title: When disaster strikes, Medicaid work rules add barriers
item.description: Medicaid provides a critical safety net for people to maintain healthcare coverage. But new work requirements create barriers for those trying to recover from natural disasters.

item.title: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran
item.description: Despite rising tension, President Trump told an Israeli outlet he may not make a decision on his next move in the Iran war until 2027.

item.title: Army plans to carry out detonation at Iowa plant on Wednesday
item.description: The Department of the Army said it plans to use an emergency munitions and explosives exclusion to the Environmental Protection Agency's permit.

item.title: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and sports broadcaster, dies at 75
item.description: Tom Jackson, a former Denver Broncos player and ESPN analyst, has died at 75.

item.title: Hall of Fame sports broadcaster Tom Jackson dies at 75
item.description: The Denver Broncos announced that Hall of Fame sports broadcaster Tom Jackson has died at 75.

item.title: "I Have a Dream" pages written by Martin Luther King Jr. to go up for auction
item.description: Martin Luther King Jr. wrote his famous "I Have a Dream" speech on yellow legal paper in long cursive in blue ink. Those pages have been tucked away until now; they are headed to auction in January. Brian Unger has the story.

item.title: Kate Middleton shares cancer journey details in surprise documentary
item.description: Britain's Princess of Wales, Kate Middleton, shared new details about her cancer journey in a surprise documentary previewed this weekend. Leigh Kiniry reports from London.

item.title: Consumers expected to set Cyber Monday spending record this year
item.description: Americans are expected to spend big in this year's holiday shopping season, even as they struggle with the high costs of everyday needs. Akiko Fujita reports from the Glendale Galleria near Los Angeles.

item.title: U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate
item.description: COP31, the latest installment of the United Nations' annual climate conference, ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed.

item.title: International climate talks fall apart over fossil fuels
item.description: International climate talks collapsed in Turkey on Sunday in a bitter clash over fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

item.title: ICE officers arrest 2 passengers boarding flight in Seattle
item.description: Masked immigration officers arrested two passengers on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding Saturday

item.title: Unmarked ICE agents make violent arrest at Seattle airport
item.description: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrest was caught on camera as passengers were boarding an Alaska Airlines flight. The event was so distressing that some of the crew members asked to be replaced. Olivia Rinaldi reports.

item.title: Delta Air Lines hit with delays after baggage network system issue
item.description: The Delta Air Lines delays are most impacting flights in and out of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport in Georgia.

item.title: Army moves forward with plans to detonate 5 tons of toxic materials in Iowa
item.description: The Army warned that freezing temperatures could risk an accidental toxic explosion at a munitions plant in Middletown, Iowa. The Trump administration declared an emergency and is moving ahead with a plan to blow up the unstable explosives despite a federal court order. Ian Lee has more on the controversial plan.

item.title: Delta Air Lines says it's resolved network issue, but severe weather could cause more delays
item.description: Delta Air Lines said it resolved an automation outage that disrupted half of all flights, but the weather is creating another speed bump for the Thanksgiving travel rush. Shanelle Kaul reports and Andrew Kozak has the forecast.

item.title: Riding wild animals and selling crafts at a prison rodeo
item.description: Louisiana State Penitentiary hosts a rodeo where incarcerated men risk being stepped on, gored and flipped upside down. But for these volunteer, self-taught cowboys, it's all worth it.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: ​​A rodeo inside a maximum security prison
item.description: Louisiana State Penitentiary, once known as "the bloodiest prison in America," hosts a rodeo. Inmates turned self-taught cowboys leap onto wild animals for a chance to chase a feeling of freedom.

item.title: This online community of young people is idolizing mass shooters
item.description: 60 Minutes goes inside a growing, online community of young people who idolize, romanticize and sometimes even seek to emulate mass shooters.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: How cartels make new synthetic opioids
item.description: The DEA is confronting what it calls the deadliest drug threat the U.S. has faced: synthetic opioids. Drug cartels tweak one molecule at a time to evade law enforcement.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: The online community idolizing mass shooters
item.description: Researchers have identified 12 attacks in the US in the last three years that were carried out by members in the TCC, a growing online community that idolizes mass shooters.

item.title: He took a $10 synthetic opioid few have heard of. It killed him.
item.description: Nitazenes, a new class of synthetic opioid up to 80 times more potent than fentanyl, are among those being churned out by drug cartels.

item.description: Gold Star families this past week finally got some answers from the Army about the Iranian drone strike that killed their loved ones — but their search for accountability goes on.

item.title: Democrats reach historic House majority not seen since 1992
item.description: "House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM," Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York said Sunday.

item.title: Princeton student detained by ICE at Reagan Airport after conference
item.description: Eva Yi Xie, a third-year Ph.D. Princeton student, was detained following a presentation she gave at the Society for Neuroscience.
